title: Understanding the main Method
subtopics: The traditional public static void main(String[] args) form
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of understanding the main method and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—the traditional public static void main(string[] args) form—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study understanding the main method with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you understand what the compiler and runtime each do when a program is built and launched. In this lesson, focus on the traditional public static void main(string[] args) form and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: String values are immutable sequences of text. Use value equality for text content, understand Unicode code points for international text, and prefer StringBuilder for repeated concatenation in loops. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect the traditional public static void main(string[] args) form with method parameters before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: The traditional public static void main(String[] args) form
items.text: String values are immutable sequences of text. Use value equality for text content, understand Unicode code points for international text, and prefer StringBuilder for repeated concatenation in loops.

items.title: Method parameters
items.text: A method gives a named contract to a unit of behavior. Keep responsibilities focused, define clear parameter and return types, and test typical, boundary, and invalid cases independently.

items.title: The role of static
items.text: The normal workflow is source file → compiler → class file → JVM execution. Compilation errors are reported before the program runs; runtime exceptions and logical mistakes require different debugging approaches. Apply that reasoning specifically to the role of static and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.
